newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt moribund, awaits US jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt moribund, awaits US jobs data.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were narrowly mixed in an extremely thin market as players awaited key U.S. economic data due out Friday.

"I think contrary to the equity markets, our markets have been very quiet. I think everyone is waiting on tomorrow's figures," said Kurt Schmid, managing director of emerging markets trading at SBC Warburg in New York.
At 1730 EST/2230 GMT, Argentine FRBs were 1/8 lower at 89-5/8 bid, while Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/8 firmer at 75 bid and Mexican pars were 1/4 stronger at 70-3/4 bid.
Market experts said the March U.S. employment report will provide a much clearer picture of whether the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates further.

"Very clearly, if the market anticipates that there is not just one tightening move by the Fed in May but a couple thereafter, it could lead to further corrections and I think tomorrow's figure and particularly hourly earnings will set the tone for the time being," said Schmid.
According to a Reuters poll, U.S. economists forecast U.S. payrolls rose by 196,000 in March, down from 339,000 new jobs in February.

Though the upgrade of Argentina and Brazil by Standard & Poor's on Wednesday continued to receive wide applause by the market, trading sources said the news was clearly overshadowed by nervousness about the upcoming jobs report.

"Clearly the market's reaction to the upgrades was muted because everyone is waiting to see what the picture is for the interest rate scenario," said one emerging markets trader at a major U.S. investment house.
"In spite of the fact that it was probably anticipated, it was very good news," said Schmid who noted, however, that the price gains were relatively insignificant.

Schmid said that if the upgrades by S&P had been done in a firm market, the news probably would have driven prices up about one to two percentage points on both Argentine and Brazilian debt instruments.
Among Eastern European debt, Bulgaria IAB's rose 1/8 to 57-3/4 bid, while Russian Vneshekonombank dollar loans fell 7/8 to 77-1/8 bid.
